result.instructions: Long-term memory: what this person or team worked on, wrote, decided and said, and what was learned from it. Search it before answering about past work, people, decisions or dates, and open a result to read it whole. Save what is worth remembering later: a decision and why, a preference, a fact about a person or a system.

Long-term memory: what this person or team worked on, wrote, decided and said, and what was learned from it. Search it before answering about past work, people, decisions or dates, and open a result to read it whole. Save what is worth remembering later: a decision and why, a preference, a fact about a person or a system.

tools.name: memory_search
tools.description: Search memory: everything it was given (e-mails, messages, notes, documents, conversations, commits, …) and what was learned from them — facts, decisions, dated events, profiles of people and things. Best first; each result with its date and id. Ask in plain words, as you would ask a colleague who read it all. Name dates when the question names a time. Open a result with memory_open for all of it.

query.description: What you need to know, in plain words.

limit.description: How many of each to return — dated observations, and other memories (default 20; 100 to 200 when you gather everything on a topic, list or count things, or need their dates).

order.description: Best first (default), or oldest first — for what happened when, and in what order.

from.description: Only what happened on or after this date (YYYY-MM-DD, YYYY-MM or YYYY) — when the request names a time ("in June 2023", "last week").

to.description: Only what happened on or before this date (YYYY-MM-DD, YYYY-MM or YYYY).

tools.name: memory_open
tools.description: Read one memory item whole, by the id memory_search or memory_explore gave: everything it holds, when it happened, and for something learned, the records it was learned from.

id.description: The memory id, as memory_search or memory_explore gave it.

tools.name: memory_explore
tools.description: Explore memory around a topic, or around items you already found: it follows what they share — the same people, places, systems, names — and links between memories, to what a search for the words does not find. Returns what search found, what is related, and the concepts around it to explore next.

topic.description: What to explore, in plain words — a system, a project, a problem, a name.

from.description: Memory ids to explore from, as memory_search or memory_explore gave them.

limit.description: How many related items to return (default 10).

tools.name: memory_save
tools.description: Save something to memory, to be found later by memory_search: a decision and why, a preference, a fact about a person, a project or a system, what was learned. Write it to be understood on its own, later, by someone who was not here: name who and what, and the date when it matters.

text.description: What to remember, written to be understood on its own.

title.description: A short title (default: the start of the text).
